ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure is a "tower"-shaped composite figure. The upper part is an equilateral triangle, the middle is a horizontal rectangle, and the lower part is a square. The base of the equilateral triangle exactly coincides with the entire upper side of the rectangle; the square is connected below the rectangle. The vertical arrow with a question mark on the right marks the height of the rectangle; the nearby label 9 cm indicates the side length of the square. Reasoning: The side length of the square is 9 cm, so the perimeter of the square is 4×9=36 cm. The three figures have the same perimeter, so the perimeter of the equilateral triangle is also 36 cm. Each side of the equilateral triangle is 36÷3=12 cm, so its base length is 12 cm. From the image, this base is also the length of the rectangle. The perimeter of the rectangle is also 36 cm. Let the height of the rectangle be h, then 2(12+h)=36, giving 12+h=18, so h=6 cm.

method.method_draft: First describe the image: the tower has a top equilateral triangle whose base is exactly the full top edge of the horizontal rectangle; the square is attached below the rectangle; the marked unknown is the rectangle’s vertical side/height. From the text, the square side is 9 cm and all three shapes have equal perimeter. Compute the square perimeter as 4×9=36 cm. Since the triangle is equilateral and has the same perimeter, each triangle side, including its base, is 36÷3=12 cm. By the image, that base is also the rectangle’s length. The rectangle perimeter is also 36 cm, so 2(12+h)=36. Solve h=6 cm.

method.method_draft: Weakly distinct algebraic/semiperimeter method. First describe the image: the unknown arrow marks the height of the middle rectangle, and the top edge of that rectangle is shared with the base of the equilateral triangle. Let the common perimeter be P. From the text and image, the square has side 9 cm, so P=4·9=36. The rectangle’s semiperimeter is P/2=18, meaning its width plus height equals 18. The rectangle’s width is the equilateral triangle’s side because the triangle base sits exactly on the rectangle’s top edge; since the triangle perimeter is P, that width is P/3=12. Therefore the unknown rectangle height is 18−12=6 cm.
